sentences.text: The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.

The brief facts of the petitioner's case are as under:
2.

That on 02-08-2020 at about 8-30 a.m. the petitioner was proceeding in a motor cycle Honda CB Shine bearing registration No.KA-53/EW-3202 as a pillion rider from Paramanahalli via Kattigenahalli on the extreme left side of the road, when they reached near Khajihosahalli village, Jadigenahalli Hobli, Hosakote Taluk, Bengaluru Dist., at that time, driver of Tata Ace Gold bearing registration No.KA-53/D- 5693 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner, came at high speed from opposite direction and dashed against the petitioner's motor cycle and caused the accident.
Due to forced impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

3. It is further stated that, immediately the petitioner was shifted to MVJ Medical College and Research Hospital, Hoskote, Bengaluru wherein he was treated as an inpatient and undergone surgery and spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards medicines, attendant charges, food and nourishment etc.
4.

sentences.text: It is also stated in the petition that, prior to the accident the petitioner was hale, healthy and working as a mason and was earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month and he used to spend the said amount for the maintenance of his family members.
Due to accidental injuries he could do his day to day work as earlier to the accident.
5. It is alleged in the petition that, the accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent act of the driver of the Tata Ace Gold bearing registration No.KA-53/D-5693.
Hence, the Thirumalashettihalli Police have registered criminal case against driver of the offending vehicle in Crime No.72/2020 under section 279 and 338 of IPC.
As such, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, the petitioner has filed the instant petition, seeking compensation.
6. After registration of the case, notices were issued to the respondents.

In response to the notices,
the respondent No.1 & 2 have appeared through their respective counsel and filed the written statements.

7. In the written statement the respondent No.1 stated that, he is the RC owner of the Tata Ace Gold bearing registration No.KA-53/D-5693 and he insured his vehicle with respondent No.2, as on the date of the accident the policy was in force.

Further, contended that, this accident occurred due to sole negligence on the part of the petitioner, hence the petition is bad for non joinder of necessary Thyagaraj vs Ravi Kumar.A on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195988521/
2 parties, i.e., owner and insurer of the petitioner's motor cycle.
Further denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner and expenses incurred towards medical and other incidental charges.
Further contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive, exaggerated and arbitrary.
With all these main grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition with cost.

8. In the written statement of the respondent No.2 has stated that this respondent is the insurer of the Tata Ace Gold bearing registration No.KA- 53/D-5693 and the liability of this respondent is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
Further contended that offending vehicle was not at all involved in the accident.
It is also contention of the respondent No.2 that the driver of the offending vehicle had no valid and effective driving licence, hence there is a violation of terms and conditions of the policy.

This respondent took specific contention that, as on the date of the accident the petitioner does not posses valid D.L. and also not wearing the ISI mark helmet, hence this accident occurred due to sole negligence on the part of the petitioner.
Further denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner and expenses incurred towards medical and other incidental charges.

Ultimately, contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive,
exaggerated and arbitrary.
With all these main grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition with cost.

9. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the parties, this court has framed the following issues;
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioner proves that, he sustained grievous injuries in an motor vehicle accident,
that was taken place on 02.08.2020 at about 8-30 a.m. near Khajihosahalli village, Jadigenahalli Hobli, Hosakote Taluk, Bengaluru due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Tata Ace Gold bearing registration No.KA-53/D-5693 in an actionable negligence?
2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for?

If so, at what rate? from whom?
3) What order or award?

sentences.text:
Before appreciation of the evidence placed by the Petitioner about the injuries sustained by her,
in the accident and its consequences, it is apt to note herein, the preposition laid down in the following land mark judgment, while appreciating the injury cases in Motor Vehicle Act.
Civil Appeal No.8981/2010 D.D. 18.10.2010 Rajkumar V/s Ajay Kumar & Another of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India.
"In the aforesaid case, it was held that, the court has to make judicious attempt to award compensation to the loss suffered by the claimant.
The compensation should not be assessed conservatively.
On the other hand, compensation should also not be endeavouring to secure some uniformity and consistency.
The object of awarding compensation is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done, as far as money can do so, in a fair reasonable and equitable manner."

"while determining quantum of compensation, in such cases, the court has to strike a balance between the inflated and unreasonable demands of a victim and the equally untenable claim of the opposite party saying that nothing is payable.
That sympathy for the victim does not, and should not, comes in the way of making a correct assessment.
But if a case is made out, and the court must not be chary of awarding adequate compensation.
PW1 has stated in his evidence that, he has sustained the injuries in a road traffic accident.
In connection with the injuries he has produced wound certificate marked as Ex.P5.

The said document discloses that, he had sustained the following injuries:-
Open fracture of right distal femur 43.
The doctor opined that the above said injury is grievous in nature.

The petitioner has produced discharge summaries marked at Ex.P7, which shows that the petitioner was admitted on 2.8.2020 and discharged on 1.9.2020 again from 2.12.2020 to 12.12.2020 from 17.2.2021 to 23.2.2021.
Apart from his evidence placed the evidence of MRD, MVJ Medical College as PW2.
He has placed authorisation letter, MLC extract, police intimation and inpatient record as per Ex.P13 to Ex.P16.
In addition to his evidence palced the evidence of Dr.S.A.Somashekar as PW5.
He has stated in his evidence that the petitioner has sustained fracture GA type II of distal femur (right) with inter condylar extension and underwent surgeries.
He has placed OPD and x-ray as per Ex.P17 & Ex.P18.

By taking into consideration of the nature of the injury and the treatment taken by the petitioner, he could have undergone pain and sufferings while taking treatment, as an in patient as well as an outpatient.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.30,000/- under the head of Pain and Sufferings.
Loss of income during treatment period:
44. PW1 has stated that, he was working as a mason-cum-agriculturist and earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.

In this regard, he has not placed any iota of Thyagaraj vs Ravi Kumar.A on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195988521/
8 documents to prove his actual income.

During the period of treatment definitely, there was some difficulty to do his daily routine work and to do his work for livelihood at least for a period of four months by looking in to the nature of the injuries sustained by him.

Medical Expeneses;

towards medical expenses.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.40,000/- towards attendant charges, food,
nourishment and conveyance charges.

Loss of future income;
47.
The petitioner herein, asserting that, he had sustained permanent disability, consequent upon the injuries sustained by him.
In order to prove the same, the petitioner has relied on his evidence along with the wound certificate and other medical documents.

In the evidence of the PW1,
reiterated the same thing forthcoming in the main petition.

As already discussed above, wound certificate placed by him as per Ex.P5 and other medical documents goes to show that, he had sustained grievous injuries for which he took the treatment as an inpatient.
Apart from this, another material witness by name Dr.S.A.Somashekar examined as PW5.

PW5 has stated in his evidence that the petitioner has sustained Open fracture GA type II of distal femur right with inter condylar extension and underwent wound debridement, Ex. fix application and Ex.fix removal (tibial pins).

He has placed outpatient record, and x-ray as per Ex.P17 & Ex.P18.
48.

PW5 has stated that, at the time of his examination the petitioner was walks with pain and limping, diffuse swelling of right thigh and wasting of right leg, surgical scars are seen over right hip.

At the time of cross-examination of PW5, stated that he is not the treated doctor and fracture is united.
Further stated that based on the documents he has assessed the physical disability.
This witness also denied the suggestion that, he assessed the disability of the petitioner on higher side.

50. Over all appreciation of evidence of PW5 along with the entire medical documents the whole body disability expressed by PW5 as right lower limb is 72% and whole body is 36% seems little bit exorbitant.
Hence, by taking into consideration of point of disability expressed by PW5, it is apt to take whole body disability as 23% instead of 36%.
The same will meets the ends of justice.
51. In connection with the age of the petitioner is concerned, on going through the cause title of the petition reveals that, as on the date of the petition, his age was 32 years.

In support of the age proof,
he has placed Aadhar card marked at Ex.P8 for consideration.
On going through the said documents, the date of birth of the petitioner has been mentioned as 1.6.1998.
The accident occurred on 2.8.2020.
Therefore, as on the date of accident, the age of the petitioner is considered as 32 years.
To the said age as per Sarla Verma case, multiplier '16' is to be taken into consideration.

52. Next factual aspect of the income of the petitioner is concerned, in his evidence the petitioner has stated that, prior to the accident, he was doing mason work and also doing agriculture and getting an income of Rs.20,000/- per month.
The petitioner has not placed any documents to show that he was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
In such a situation, as per law notional income has to be taken into consideration.
But the said notional income is to be taken judiciously, by taking into consideration of the year of the accident.
It is pertinent to note that, in the case on hand, the alleged accident had taken place in the year 2020.
As per the notional income chart, I am of the view that, it is apt to take the notional income of the petitioner as Rs.14,500/- for the year 2020.

53. In the light of my detailed discussions held above, no doubt injuries sustained by the petitioner,
definitely come in the way of his future, in a slight manner, to do his daily routine work, as well as to do his work for livelihood on going through his age criteria.

Hence, the petitioner herein, is entitled for compensation under loss of future income as follows:
Rs.14,500 X 12 X 16 X 23/100= Rs.6,40,320/-
Loss of amenities;
54.

PW1 has stated in his evidence that, due to accidental injuries he is completely bed ridden,
cannot walk, stand cannot lift or carry weight, cannot ride vehicle as prior to the accident.
On perusal of evidence of PW5 and also medical documents, I am of the view that, the petitioner will suffer a slight problem in future also to do his normal work, as well as his work for livelihood.
Hence, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.40,000/- towards loss of amenities.
55. In connection with the future medication, PW5 has stated in his evidence that, the petitinoer needs surgery for control of infection and achieving union, which would cost around Rs.1,00,000/-.

Relying on the opinion of the doctor it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.30,000/-
under the head of future medical expenses.
